dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Yeah, hi, is this the, um, is somebody actually there? It's Sunday, I didn't think anybody would pick up.
Yep, somebody's here. Storm line's open today. What's going on?

What's going on is my garage is under water, that's what's going on. I was in the middle of a nice nap, a really nice nap, first one I've had in weeks, and I get up and there's water coming down the driveway like a river. [line breaks up] ...can you hear me?
I lost you for a second there. You said water coming down the driveway. Can you give me your name and the address?
Donna Fiore. 452 Annandale Road, up in the North End. I run my business out of there, well, I store things there, for the business.
Okay, Donna Fiore, 452 Annandale. And the water's coming from where, do you know?

The catch basin at the corner! It's packed solid with leaves. Wet leaves, a whole mat of them sitting on top of the grate. I've looked at it since October. So the rain comes, it can't go down, and it backs right up and runs into my driveway and into the garage.
Got it. Catch basin at the corner, clogged with leaves, backing up toward your driveway. Is it the corner of Annandale and a cross street, or is it right in front of your place?
It's the corner right next to my house. Maybe forty feet. Well, no, I'm saying that wrong, it's closer to thirty. Whatever, you can see it from my front steps.
Okay, thirty feet or so from your steps. And you said the garage took water. How bad?

Bad! I had furniture stored in there. Good furniture, pieces I was going to sell. Upholstered stuff, a couple of dressers sitting on the floor. All of it's wet. Ruined. Some of it I can't even lift now it's so soaked. [line breaks up] ...and nobody from the city ever came to clean that thing out.
I'm sorry, that's a mess. Did you call about this basin before today?

Did I call? I mean, I thought about it a hundred times, I should have called in the fall, I'm not going to lie. But it's a city drain. It's your job to look at it before it's raining sideways. That's what the leaf thing is for, isn't it?
Fair enough. I'm pulling up what I can see here. Is the water still coming in right now, or has it slowed?
It's still coming. It's snow and rain mixed, the snow's turning to slush, and that slush is making it worse. It's blocking the whole... [inaudible] ...are you there?
Still here. You cut out on slush blocking the whole something.
The whole gutter along the curb. The slush is packing in with the leaves.
Okay. Is anybody in danger, anything electrical in the garage, or is it just the water and the stored stuff?
Well, there's a freezer out there, but it's up on blocks. Oh, and you asked about danger. No. No danger, nobody's hurt. It's the stuff. It's thousands of dollars of stuff.

Understood. So here's what I'm writing down: Donna Fiore, 452 Annandale Road, catch basin at the corner clogged with leaves, water backing into the driveway and the garage, stored furniture damaged. That right?
That's right. Now what I want to know is, are you opening a work order? An actual one. And for what date? Because I'm not taking a vague answer.

Yes, I'll open the work order now, it'll be logged today, Sunday. As for when a crew gets out there, during a storm like this they go to the worst flooding first, roads and underpasses. Your basin is going to be in the queue, probably Monday or Tuesday once the rain tapers off.
Monday or Tuesday. So the work order is dated today. Today, the twenty-fifth.
Today, the twenty-fifth. I'll put that in the note so there's no argument about it.
Good. Because I'm telling you right now, if nobody calls me back today, I'm emailing every single member of the city council and the mayor's office. Every one of them. I'll attach pictures.
That's your call, Donna, and I get it. I'll flag it for a callback. What's the best number? I have to be sure I've got it right.
It's 401-555-0174. That's my cell, but the reception out here is lousy, so if it drops, just try again.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-four. Right?
Yes. Zero-one-seven-four. And call today, not tomorrow.

I'll mark it for today. Whoever's on the storm desk this evening should be reaching out. In the meantime, if you can safely get to the grate with a rake or shovel, clearing some leaves can help, but only if it's safe and you're not standing in moving water.
In this weather? In my slippers? No. That's why I'm calling you.
Fair. Then just keep clear of it. Take photos of the garage and the basin while you're at it.
Oh, I've got photos. I've been taking them all afternoon.
Good. Hang onto those. Anything else I can add to the ticket?
Just that this is not the first time that corner has backed up, and it's going to keep happening unless somebody does something. Put that in. Please.
I'll note it. Backs up at that corner repeatedly. Okay, you're all set on the ticket. Somebody will call you.
Fine. Thank you, Kevin. Today. Remember.
Today. Stay dry, Donna.
